To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fiber based polarization sensitive OCT systems using a PMF with a specific polarization axis orientation as sample arm fiber are insensitive to fiber motion induced fiber birefringenet variations for determining the optic axis orientation.

we propose a fiber based PS OCT system that can extract sample optic axis orientation correctly by using polarization maintaining fiber (slow axis orientation) as the sample arm, and that the fiber birefrigence variation does not affect the accuracy of the optic axis orientation determination.

we propose the use fiber based polarization sensitive OCT with polarization maintaining fiber to extract the relative optic axis information in fibrous tissues, which are insensitive to the fiber motion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a fiber motion insensitive fiber based PS OCT system for optic axis determination in biological tissue imaging.
the development of an optic axis determination algorithm that can be used in fiber based PS-OCT systems with a sample arm fiber that can be moved during the measurement.
the development of a fiber based polarization sensitive OCT system that is insensitive to fiber motion, and can be used to accurately measure the optic axis orientation of fibrous biological tissue.

a fiber with a constant birefringent axis can be used for fiber based PS OCT to extract sample optic axis orientation without any ambiguity.
the fiber birefrigence in a PS OCT system can have a significant effect on the accuracy of determining the optic axis orientation, and this effect can be removed by using the proposed method.
fiber motion insensitive fiber based PS OCT is possible when the PMF is used as the sample arm polarization controller.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fiber motion insensitivity PS OCT system can be achieved by using the PMF with a special polarization orientation as the sample fiber.

the use of the PM fiber as the system fiber for PS OCT imaging of fibrous tissues is an effective approach to remove the fiber birefringing induced offset ambiguity from the determination of the sample optic axis orientation.
the proposed method could be used to extract optic axis orientation of fibrous biological tissue using fiber based PS-OCT system with PMF as sample fiber.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of the PMFs with the slow or fast polarization axis orientation can be used to extend the application of the previously reported algorithm for determining the relative optic axis orientations in fiber based PS-OCT systems to situations in which there are fiber motion induced changes of the system fiber parameters.

the proposed method can be used to determine optic axis orientation with a PMF based fiber PS-OCT system, which is insensitive to fiber motion and fiber birefrigence variations, which are common in fiber-based PS-OCT imaging.
the fiber birefrigence can be used as an internal reference for determining optic axis orientations in fiber based PS-OCT systems.
